messages:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's continuous-batching tweak I see a perf regression concentrated on short prompts (seq <= 32). p99 generation latency up ~22% on the small-prompt cohort. See quick numbers: baseline p99=120ms -> post-change p99=146ms.

aj: ugh. Is this for hosted only or across dedicated/private too?

maria: Repro on dedicated (staging) and hosted. The bigger batches for short prompts seems to push kernels into a slower path. Attaching a tiny flame snippet.

maria: ```
flame: small_prompt_case
- kernel_dispatch (45%)
- kv_cache_lookup (12%)
- cuda_kernel_q8_fallback (28%)
- rpc_overhead (5%)
- other (10%)
```

aj: cuda_kernel_q8_fallback stands out. If kernel selector is routing some seq<=32 jobs to a fallback (float32 or slower q8 implementation) when the batch mixes with medium seq, that would explain it. Did the heuristic change the kernel affinity rules?

maria: The change groups batches by decode_rate_bucket and then by age, we loosened strict kernel affinity to increase batch sizes. Looks like that loosen -> kernel mismatch.

kevin: Also saw KV prefetch thrash on these workloads. Short prompts are decode-bound and touch the KV often; larger mixed batches increase live set and push L2 misses. Perf counters show L2 miss rate +18% on the slow runs.

kevin: sample perf snippet: ```
L2_MISSES: 1.18e6
DRAM_BW: 42GB/s
SM_OCCUPANCY: 62%
```

sara: Can we try a policy that enforces kernel affinity but keeps batching by decode_rate only? E.g. classify workload into prompt_length_buckets first, select kernel profile, then allow cross-age batching only if kernel profile matches.

aj: Proposed quick config patch: ```yaml
batching:
  classifier:
    prompt_length_buckets: ["<=32", "33-128", ">128"]
    decode_rate_buckets: ["<=8", "9-24", ">24"]
  queue_policy:
    small_prompts: {token_budget: 64, kernel_affinity: true, age_priority: true}
    med_prompts: {token_budget: 128, kernel_affinity: false}
```

jules: I'll run A/B with token_budget=64 for small_prompts + kernel_affinity=true. Expectation: smaller batches but all on q8 kernel path -> lower p99 even if throughput drops slightly.

maria: If that fixes p99 we can try relaxing affinity with a kernel-compatibility check (only merge batches if kernels are compatible).

aj: Note: we should also instrument the selector to emit which kernel was chosen per-batch + the classifier bucket. Add a metric like `batch_kernel: q8_v2` and `bucket: small/med/large`.

infra-bot: Deployed experiment config to staging: <https://internal.redwood/p/exp/462|exp/462> :rocket:

kevin: One more thought — kv_cache prefetch size is proportional to batch token_budget. If we lower token_budget for short prompts we reduce live cache working set. Try token_budget 48 vs 64 in the A/B.

sara: Agreed. Also want to add a quick profiler that samples decode_rate per-connection to feed online classifier so thresholding adapts slowly (EWMA).

maria: Action items: (1) jules run A/B with token_budget 48/64 + kernel_affinity=true, (2) aj add batch_kernel and bucket metrics, (3) kevin add L2 miss counter to perf dashboard, (4) sara prototype EWMA-based decode_rate classifier.

jules: On it, kicking off runs now. Will post p50/p95/p99 and perf counters in this thread once done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: thanks — if we see regressions persist we may need to revert the loosened grouping and instead implement a kernel-compatibility merge step.

aj: ack. Good find, thanks for flagging. :thumbsup:
